value.first: Day 1-2: Ditch the diaper during waking hours and put her in underwear or bare-bottom at home. Offer the potty every 45-60 minutes, and always right after she wakes and 20 minutes after drinks. Keep the sits short, under 5 minutes, and celebrate any pee that lands, even a little. Expect several accidents a day at first - that is not going backward, that is how she learns the signal.
value.second: Day 3-5: You'll start to see her pause, squirm, or grab herself before she goes. When you spot it, calmly walk her to the potty. Stretch the offers to every 90 minutes or so and let her tell you. Stay in undies on outings if you can, with a spare set in the bag. Naps and nights stay in a diaper for now - daytime dryness comes first, and night can be months later.
value.third: Week 2: Most families see daytime accidents drop to one or none a day by now, with her heading to the potty more on her own. Keep the tone easy - accidents still happen when she's busy playing, so a quick reminder helps. If after two weeks she's fighting every sit or holding her stool, pause a few weeks and try again; that resistance usually means not-quite-ready, not failure. Painful or held bowel movements are worth raising with your doctor.
